VERDICT: PASS

Round 3's single blocker is closed on this head, and closed by more than the disclosure route it offered. Two of the three named Gate 8 gaps were **implemented** rather than disclosed: `expectedVersion` fencing on the run's append-only history length (`postgres-maintenance.ts::staleVersion`, `VERSION_MISMATCH` in the CHECK, the union, and `durableKernelContract.maintenanceFencedOn`, pinned by `beta08-reaction.test.ts` and driven by kernel test 10, which reads a version, moves the run with a claim, gets the stale command refused, confirms `cancellationRequested` is still false, then applies the same command at the current version); and append-only enforcement on the maintenance audit (`durable_maintenance_commands_append_only`, driven by protocol test 3's three new statements). The third — maintenance Authority — is now narrower claim 8, naming the properties shipped, the property absent, the owning slice, and the forward-compatible seam, with criterion 10 restated to its proven scope and `actor` changed from `DurableActor` to a brand-checked `Principal`.

The census now reconciles: I counted 12 kernel + 9 worker + 5 protocol = 26, matching both the record's enumeration and the manifest's verification entry. Round 3's observations 2, 5, and 6 are also closed (kernel test 11 drives the non-running `cancelRun` branch; kernel test 12 drives `createDurableRunHandle`'s `if (!lookup)` path; the unrelated evidence-record reformatting is gone from the diff). Both baselines reproduce their budgets mechanically — `ceil(400.075 × 5 / 500) × 500 = 2500` and `ceil(330.045 × 6 / 1000) × 1000 = 2000` — and the manifest, the record, and the baselines report the same figures. All sixteen criteria have driving evidence in the packet.

## Non-blocking observations

1. **Criterion 4 names four fenced surfaces; the falsification covers three and no test drives the fourth.** `postgres-effects.ts::fenced()` is a separate `SELECT 1 … AND current_attempt_id = $3 AND lease_token_digest = $4` site, but the recorded falsification says "in all three compare-and-set sites," which are `terminal`, `scheduleRetry`, and `heartbeat` in `postgres-kernel.ts`. Kernel test 1 asserts the stale holder's `succeed`, `fail`, `cancel`, and `heartbeat` are all fenced; nothing invokes an effect on a stale claim and asserts `DurableLeaseLost`. The gap is benign under at-least-once (a stale `reserve` only prevents a redundant provider call), but "effect write compares the current attempt and the lease token" rests on code reading.

2. **The expected-version fence cannot see an applied `retryRun`.** `retryRun`'s applied branch updates `durable_runs` without appending a history event, so `event_sequence` — the value both `inspect()` and `staleVersion` read — is unchanged. An operator holding version V on a `failed` run whose sibling already retried it will pass the version check and apply `cancelRun` to a `ready` run. Idempotency still holds through the state precondition (`RUN_NOT_FAILED`), and the audit records the true `stateBefore`, so nothing is lost — but criterion 10's "a command bound to a stale reading is refused with `VERSION_MISMATCH`" is universal where the mechanism is not.

3. **The new `Principal` brand refusal has no driving case, and its stated trust property is weaker than it reads.** `actorOf` throws `"durable maintenance requires a trusted Principal"` on an unbranded value; every test passes `prepared.principal` from the relocated fixture's own `questpie`. The record's argument — "a trusted `Principal` whose brand only the application's own `questpie` module can mint" — is true of the brand but not of the trust: any server-side caller holding `app.durable` also holds `framework.principal.user({ id: … })` and can mint any actor. The real containment is the sentence beside it ("server-side only, reachable through the application object rather than any generated client"), which is accurate.

4. **The record's falsification rule is now universal in phrasing and partial in practice.** "Every repair is falsified against the unrepaired code, and the exact assertion that fails is recorded with it" is followed by four instances — the fence predicate, `RUN_AS_DENIED`, `VALIDATION_FAILED`, and the cancellation tightening. Neither round 2's repairs (effect events, `transitions` correction, the criterion-14 Fetch gate) nor round 3's (expected-version fencing, the maintenance append-only trigger) received one. Both new tests assert codes the unrepaired code cannot produce, so they are self-evidently driving; the shortfall is in the record's own audit trail.

5. **The deferral's assigning authority is not pinned.** Narrower claim 8 rests on "the minimal Studio slice that ADR-0003 and ADR-0014 assign the Policy-protected inspection and maintenance protocol." Neither ADR is in `authorityDocuments`, nor in the record's own Authority header (which instead names ADR-0017 and `docs/v4/context-and-policy.md`, also unpinned). The assignment is coherent with pinned authority — Gate 8 is titled "Execution Envelope and Studio" and ADR-0021 lists minimal Studio among the beta.1 slices — but a reviewer cannot check it from this packet.

6. **Criterion 15's enumeration is partial.** "The design record discloses every claim narrower than the accepted contract:" is followed by five items; the record carries nine. The four omitted from the recitation include the maintenance-Authority disclosure that round 3's blocker produced. The criterion's substantive assertion holds and criterion 10 points at the Authority gap directly, so a reader is not misled — but the colon reads as exhaustive.

7. **Round 1 blocker 11's second clause was never demonstrated.** Its repair was "drop `network: true` **and keep the widened candidate authority scoped to the Reaction-owned path**." The first half is closed and driven (worker test 8's 404 plus the sibling 200). `message-policy.ts` still widens `candidate.kind` to `["delivered", "published"]` for every path into `messageEvents`, and the packet contains nothing stating the exposure of the lowered `mutation:messageEvents.create` that `beta01-generated-contract.test.ts` shows exists. Round 3 judged this most likely fine; one wire-absence assertion would settle it and has now been open for three rounds.

8. **The `beta08-durable-worker` budget sits on a quantization boundary.** 400.075 ms is 0.075 ms above the point where `ceil(x × 5 / 500) × 500` steps from 2000 to 2500, so a 0.6% measurement drift from round 3's 397.655 loosened the budget by 25%. The derivation is mechanical and asserted in-test, so nothing is misreported; the budget is simply unstable at this observation.

9. **`cancellationRequested` is appended but never asserted.** Kernel tests 4, 7, and 10 all execute the `cancelRun`-on-a-running-run path, so criterion 16's "every declared event kind is appended" holds by execution, but no test reads it back from `events()` the way worker tests 1 and 3 pin `effectSettled`, `effectAmbiguous`, and `ambiguityAcknowledged`.

10. **Carried forward unchanged, fourth round:** drain is implemented but undriven (`beginDrain()` executes through `close()` in every `afterAll`, but nothing asserts that a draining worker's `poll()` returns empty); "The changed loop stays under 5 s" has no recorded measurement; the manifest records which gates ran but not which head each covers (`d0aedd54` differs from repair head `f7fd0968` by manifest bytes, which the recorded `quality:release` therefore did not exercise); `quality/format-baseline.txt` pre-registers `REVIEW-04.json`, absent at this head; both CI lanes are `PENDING_CI` in the baselines while the manifest does not say the Gate 10 selected-PR and nightly lanes are unmet; the selected-PR micro scenario still needs PostgreSQL and a full application build, against Gate 10's "quick and stable"; `beta08-internal-protocol.test.ts` still drops the shared `questpie_internal` schema in `beforeEach`/`afterAll` and `helpers/beta08-durable.ts` still terminates every other backend, with nothing in-tree proving the lane is sequential; `beta05-runtime-client.test.ts` still declares its local `message.recordDelivery` with `network: true` (inert — `validateRuntimeExecutableBindings` does not compare `network` and the harness takes its wire from the compiled fixture); `postgres-maintenance.ts::appendEvent` still inserts `bumped?.sequence` with no null guard; the effect-ledger/maintenance lock-order inversion (`durable_effects` → `durable_runs` versus `durable_runs FOR UPDATE` → `durable_effects`) remains untested; `ON DELETE CASCADE` is now unreachable for `durable_maintenance_commands` as well as `durable_run_events`, further constraining the disclosed-as-absent retention story; and the contention scenario's margin still depends on the fixture's unasserted seeded message count, though the load script fails loudly rather than silently if it flips.

11. **Minor, unexplained:** PostgreSQL 18 reports 108 passing where 16 and 17 report 105, with no note on which three tests are version-gated; `beta01-generated-contract.test.ts` inlines `collaborationAuditContractPath` as a literal with no rationale; `decodeRuntimeArtifacts`' wire-coverage check compares identities only, not codec equality (harmless, since both artifacts are digested into the Runtime Build and derive from one compiler function); and `durablePrincipal`'s `service` round trip (`principal.service({ name: actor.id })`) is exercised by no test — the fixture only uses a user Principal.

12. Authority-document `sha256` values in `acceptance-manifest.json` were not verified; no hashing tool was available in this review environment.
